correctness.rationale: For deterministic horizons, the intervals are colorable with Δ colors. Within each color, the centered terms form bounded martingale differences because disjointness places all prior terms in the conditioning sigma-field. Conditional Hoeffding gives E exp(λ S_c) ≤ exp(2 λ² r_c). Generalized Hölder with p_c=(sum_d sqrt(r_d))/sqrt(r_c) yields a sub-Gaussian moment bound with R=(sum_c sqrt(r_c))²≤ΔN; Chernoff gives the stated two-sided constant 8. The proof covers all finite N and states the exact assumptions.

value.rationale: Maximum overlap is a natural design parameter for heterogeneous forecast lags. It can be far smaller than the largest lag: one horizon of length N together with N-1 one-step horizons has Δ=2. The theorem therefore supplies a finite-sample guarantee and an LLN criterion for sparse long-lag forecasts that a maximum-horizon substitution does not capture. The application is stated narrowly and does not claim optimality.
